title: Whose Morality Do They Speak? Unraveling Cultural Bias in Multilingual Language Models
findings: The study's findings related to religion are primarily through the 'Purity/Degradation' moral foundation, which incorporates religious values. The results showed significant variability in 'Purity' scores across different languages and models. Specifically, Table 2 indicates that scores for the 'Purity' foundation were consistently and statistically significantly higher in WEIRD (Western, Educated, Industrialized, Rich, and Democratic) language groups compared to non-WEIRD groups across all tested models, suggesting the models exhibit cultural biases related to concepts of sanctity and sacredness.

measurement_description: The benchmark measured the models' adherence to six moral foundations, one of which, 'Purity/Degradation', is explicitly described as incorporating 'religious and cultural values, focusing on preserving sanctity and avoiding contamination'. This foundation was assessed using items from the Moral Foundations Questionnaire-2 (MFQ-2).
